name: Black Rose Industries Ltd
title: Black Rose Industries Ltd - 514183 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Black Rose Q4 FY26 revenue rose 38% and EBITDA about 90% YoY, with EBITDA margin up to 11% from 9.7%, helped by stock-and-sale model and price normalisation.
summary.overview: Management said Q4 showed a sharp jump, with revenue up 38% and EBITDA up about 90%, driven by the stock-and-sale model in distribution and growth in manufacturing. For the full year, standalone revenue dipped slightly as chemical prices corrected from the start of the year through March 2026, while volumes grew in domestic distribution and acrylamide liquid and NMA. The company stayed debt-free, inventories fell, and a 125% dividend was recommended. Management declined to give FY27 EBITDA or revenue numbers, saying only that top line is targeted to grow over FY26 at current prices.

financial_highlights.change: up from 9.7% in the prior year

financial_highlights.value: about 35% of prior-year revenue; balance from distribution

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 EBITDA run-rate referenced in Q&A
financial_highlights.value: about Rs 13 crore per quarter (as cited by analyst; not disputed)

segments.name: Chemical distribution
segments.commentary: Backbone of the company; stock-and-sale model ensured uninterrupted supply through the Middle East disruption and supported Q4 revenue and margins. Merchant exports fell due to US tariffs and weaker US oil and gas offtake, though a strong export order pipeline is expected to convert in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Acrylamide liquid
segments.commentary: Capacity 32,000 MTPA, of which 20,000 MTPA is for merchant sales and the balance is captive. Volumes grew on new domestic and export customers after exiting the Morbi ceramic binder business; margins improved on raw material management. Export demand picked up in the second half of the current quarter.

segments.name: Acrylamide solid
segments.commentary: Capacity 3,600 MTPA. Volumes stable despite continued imports from China; management calls the business steady.

segments.name: N-methylol acrylamide (NMA)
segments.commentary: Capacity 2,000 MTPA. Significant volume growth in FY26; company is the sole supplier to a key Indian customer. Volumes guided stable for the coming period, with new customer additions as the focus.

segments.name: Polyacrylamide (PAM) solid
segments.commentary: In R&D and piloting; commercialisation targeted within FY27. Specialty amines project with Koei Chemicals is progressing, with an investment decision expected in the current year.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27: near-term chemical distribution demand expected to stay subdued on global uncertainty, but higher pricing should lift revenue.
Merchant exports: strong order pipeline expected to convert into a healthy Q1 performance.
Acrylamide: export demand picking up; focus on key export accounts using REACH and Turkish KKDIK pre-registration.
EBITDA in absolute terms expected to be sustainable; margin percentage to depend on prices and the Middle East situation. No FY27 EBITDA figure given (Rs 50 crore question declined).
Target to raise top line over FY26 at current market prices, driven by new distribution and manufacturing products.
capex_capacity: Acrylamide liquid capacity at 32,000 MTPA (20,000 MTPA merchant), up from an initial 10,000 MTPA plant.
PAM solid in piloting; commercialisation targeted during FY27.
Specialty amines project with Koei Chemicals: progressing as planned; decision expected in the current year.
Management did not quantify capacity added by the plant closure revocation; said it is not linked to the capacity expansion.
demand_pricing: Chemical prices fell steadily through February 2026, then acrylonitrile prices spiked in March with the Middle East war; the company said it still achieved good acrylamide realisations through the year.
Domestic volume growth was strong, supported by new customers and geographies; this offset price correction in the year.
Merchant exports were weaker on US tariff policy and reduced US oil and gas offtake.
Competition from Chinese imports persists in acrylamide solid and powder; volumes held steady.
Management said chemical prices had normalised after a long period of subdued levels and expects them to stay normal for some time.

qa_highlights.question: Are Q4 margins and EBITDA sustainable? (Madhur Rathi)
qa_highlights.answer: Margins depend on market conditions and are hard to predict long term. Absolute EBITDA should be sustainable; margin percentage is price-driven, and prices have normalised.

qa_highlights.question: Can Q4 EBITDA of about Rs 13 crore per quarter be maintained, and was it inventory gain or operating income? (Madhur Rathi)
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 was a mix of inventory gain and operating gain, with volumes rising. Only a 15-day period was affected by the war. No quarterly figure was confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of permanent revocation of the plant closure directions? (Vishwendra Singh)
qa_highlights.answer: The closure notice has been permanently revoked, so operations continue without interruption.

qa_highlights.question: Effect of new products on the top line? (Shweta Agarwal)
qa_highlights.answer: New products are being added in both distribution and manufacturing. The target is higher top line than FY26 at current prices, depending on market penetration and prices.

qa_highlights.question: Will Rs 50 crore EBITDA be achieved in FY27? (Madhur Rathi)
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number, saying too many factors drive it.

qa_highlights.question: How much capacity can the revocation add, and what revenue growth in FY27 and FY28? (Vishwendra Singh)
qa_highlights.answer: No numbers given. Management said revocation and capacity expansion are unrelated, and the aim is maximum utilisation plus pipeline products.

risks_watch: Margin sustainability: Q4 benefited from price normalisation, the stock-and-sale model, and inventory effects; management did not separate inventory gain from operating gain.
Middle East conflict: raw material (acrylonitrile) prices spiked in March 2026; duration of the war is a stated swing factor.
US tariffs: weaker merchant exports and US oil and gas offtake.
Chinese competition in acrylamide solid and powder.
Q1 FY27 distribution demand is guided subdued; revenue lift relies on pricing and export order conversion.
Dividend recorded as 125%, which needs confirming against the face value and the company's dividend policy.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and Q4 momentum, but evasive on forward numbers: management repeatedly declined to give FY27 EBITDA or revenue targets and attributed margin direction to market prices. The webinar was disrupted by technical problems, so many questions were answered via the chat board.
key_quotes: So, the margins and EBITDA are always a result of the market scenario.
So, I would rather you stay away from giving you any number.
The company is not dependent on gas in any way, while there was a small impact in some of the products in the distribution business.

adds.what: PAM solid commercialisation (in piloting; not a quantified capacity addition)
Specialty amines project with Koei Chemicals (investment decision pending; no capacity quantified)

growth.why: Management targets FY27 top line above FY26 at current prices, backed by higher pricing, a strong Q1 export order pipeline and new distribution and manufacturing products, but gave no FY27 revenue or EBITDA number and no quantified new capacity.
